title: The Sleeping Bell
premise: Paloma Dunmore has spent years perfecting the art of being unnoticed, a hospice nurse who hears the dying count backwards and knows better than to ask why. When the village of Hollowmere's church bell—melted down in 1911 after it was rung to cover a massacre—begins ringing at night, only Paloma and her dying patient, Edith Crane, can hear it. The bell is calling its debt: every family that stayed silent in 1911 owes a life, and the founders' unfinished ritual is the only way to pay it without blood. As neighbors vanish one by one, Paloma must choose between exposing the town's buried crime—which would destroy the descendants she's come to care for—or completing the ritual herself, which demands she surrender her own name, her memories, and her survival. In the end, she rings the recast bell with her own hands, trading her identity for the village's peace, and wakes as a stranger no one remembers, finally invisible on purpose.
about_author: Wendell Vane is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent a decade listening to the last words of the dying in rural England. They write horror about small communities keeping large secrets, and claim they have never once heard anyone count backwards.

chapters.title: The Counting Hour
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On her nightly rounds through Hollowmere, Paloma tends Edith Crane, who counts backwards from ninety-nine each evening—and always stops at seven, the number of families who went silent in 1911. When the melted church bell tolls across the moor, Edith whispers 'it remembers us,' and dies smiling. Emotional beat: dread taking root; Paloma realizes her invisibility has made her the only witness.

chapters.title: What the Founders Owed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, shifting to dual POV with Tom Ashford, the vicar's grandson. Digging into parish records, Paloma learns the bell was rung to drown the screams of seven murdered laborers, and the founders began a binding ritual they never finished. That night, the first descendant vanishes from his locked house. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—Tom begs her to stop digging even as he helps her.

chapters.title: Seven Names, One Debt
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax build. With three villagers gone and the bell tolling faster, Paloma and Tom find the ritual text beneath the church floor: it requires all seven descendant names spoken by someone willing to give up their own. The remaining descendants vote to sacrifice an outsider instead—a drifter. Paloma must decide whether justice outside the law is still justice. Emotional beat: moral rupture; Tom chooses truth over bloodline and sides with her.

chapters.title: Rung
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, closing with Tom's. In the belfry at midnight, Paloma speaks the seven names and rings the recast bell as the debt comes due around them. The tolling stops mid-swing; the vanished are returned, alive but hollow-eyed, and everyone forgets Paloma Dunmore ever existed—including Tom, who feels an inexplicable grief he cannot name. Emotional beat: devastating peace; survival purchased at the price of being remembered.
